body_text:
For an ordered basis $\mathcal{B} = (b_1, \dots, b_n)$ of a vector space $V$,
the *coordinate isomorphism* $[\,\cdot\,]_{\mathcal{B}} : V \to F^n$ maps
each vector $v = \sum_{i=1}^n c_i b_i$ to its unique column vector of coordinates:
$$ [v]_{\mathcal{B}} = \begin{pmatrix} c_1 \\ \vdots \\ c_n \end{pmatrix} \in F^n. $$
The coordinate vector $[v]_{\mathcal{B}}$ depends heavily on the chosen basis,
while the vector $v$ remains an invariant geometric entity.
